evidence.claim: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.title: Iran (Islamic Republic of) 1979 (rev. 1989) Constitution
evidence.excerpt: Article 110 gives the Leader supreme command of the armed forces, war-and-peace authority, and appointment power over key judiciary, media, and military posts; Article 111 provides a temporary replacement council if the office becomes vacant.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Stable constitutional text reproduced by a reputable legal repository; directly defines authority and constraints relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct office-level authority held by Ali Khamenei as Supreme Leader.
contrary_evidence: The constitution includes a formal vacancy-replacement mechanism, so the office is powerful but not literally unbounded on paper.

evidence.claim: Khamenei said Iran's future should not depend on the success or failure of nuclear talks and told officials not to let work stall because of negotiations.
evidence.title: Khamenei Says Iran's Future Should Not Be Tied to Nuclear Talks
evidence.excerpt: Khamenei said Iran's future should not depend on the success or failure of nuclear talks and told officials not to let work stall because of negotiations.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and quoted speech excerpt
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire distributed by VOA; direct quote from the ruler in the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler statement during stalled Vienna talks
contrary_evidence: This rhetoric was paired later in 2022 with reduced monitoring and additional enrichment steps.

evidence.claim: Iran's atomic energy organization agreed to provide written explanations and supporting documents on three undeclared locations by March 20, 2022, with follow-up meetings in Tehran and a goal of reporting conclusions by the June 2022 Board meeting.
evidence.title: Joint Statement by the Vice-President of Iran and the IAEA Director General
evidence.excerpt: Iran's atomic energy organization agreed to provide written explanations and supporting documents on three undeclared locations by March 20, 2022, with follow-up meetings in Tehran and a goal of reporting conclusions by the June 2022 Board meeting.
evidence.source_locator: numbered items 1-4 in the joint statement
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IAEA text with explicit dates, obligations, and follow-up steps.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 safeguards process surrounding Khamenei's nuclear posture
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional Iran-side commitment under the Supreme Leader's system; not a personal order from Khamenei on the page, but directly relevant to his authority over the file.
contrary_evidence: The same issue later remained unresolved, showing the March process did not close the safeguards gap.

evidence.claim: The IAEA reported that Iran continued enriching uranium up to 60% U-235 and that its JCPOA-related verification and monitoring were seriously affected after Iran stopped implementing its nuclear-related commitments, including the Additional Protocol.
evidence.title: Verification and monitoring in the Islamic Republic of Iran in light of UNSCR 2231 (2015)
evidence.excerpt: The IAEA reported that Iran continued enriching uranium up to 60% U-235 and that its JCPOA-related verification and monitoring were seriously affected after Iran stopped implementing its nuclear-related commitments, including the Additional Protocol.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct IAEA report in the target year with specific operational findings and monitoring consequences.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to the Iranian state under Khamenei's top-level authority over the nuclear file.
contrary_evidence: Iran maintained that its program was peaceful and that pressure from the West drove the rollback.
The report documents state-level actions, not a private decision transcript from Khamenei.

evidence.claim: Iran ordered removal of IAEA surveillance cameras and related equipment; the Director General said this removed the possibility for full confidence in future declarations and could damage assurance of the peaceful nature of Iran's nuclear program.
evidence.title: Iran Turns off Twenty-Seven Cameras
evidence.excerpt: Iran ordered removal of IAEA surveillance cameras and related equipment; the Director General said this removed the possibility for full confidence in future declarations and could damage assurance of the peaceful nature of Iran's nuclear program.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The page reproduces the contemporaneous IAEA report and captures the agency's direct assessment of the consequences.
evidence.period_fit: Immediate 2022 operational decision affecting monitoring continuity
evidence.ruler_attribution: State action under Khamenei's top-level control over the nuclear file; not a personal directive on the page.
contrary_evidence: Iran framed the move as a response to IAEA behavior rather than a reduction in safety.
The action preserved seals and storage, but still degraded continuity of knowledge.

evidence.claim: After the June camera removal, the IAEA said it could not recover continuity of knowledge and could not exclude that subsequent levels of activity were significantly different from what had previously been observed.
evidence.title: Verification and monitoring in the Islamic Republic of Iran in light of UNSCR 2231 (2015)
evidence.excerpt: After the June camera removal, the IAEA said it could not recover continuity of knowledge and could not exclude that subsequent levels of activity were significantly different from what had previously been observed.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IAEA reporting with direct statement about the monitoring gap created in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional consequence of decisions taken under Khamenei's authority over the nuclear portfolio.
contrary_evidence: The IAEA said a new baseline could eventually be established, but only after a considerable time and with uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Iran agreed to a November IAEA visit to start giving answers on uranium particles found at three sites, though diplomats said the move came before an expected new Board resolution.
evidence.title: Iran sets up meeting on IAEA inquiry as diplomatic clash looms
evidence.excerpt: Iran agreed to a November IAEA visit to start giving answers on uranium particles found at three sites, though diplomats said the move came before an expected new Board resolution.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on an explicit diplomatic step, but still mediated through a secondary publisher.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 response to the safeguards dispute
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution is to the Iranian government and nuclear authorities under Khamenei's system, not a personal Khamenei speech.
contrary_evidence: Diplomats described the visit as possibly tactical rather than a substantive breakthrough.

evidence.claim: Iran began enriching uranium to 60% at Fordow after the Board resolution, a step described as retaliation to pressure from the IAEA and Western powers.
evidence.title: Iran starts enriching uranium to 60% purity at Fordow site - official
evidence.excerpt: Iran began enriching uranium to 60% at Fordow after the Board resolution, a step described as retaliation to pressure from the IAEA and Western powers.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and Reuters explanation of the timing
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire with a direct, contemporaneous account of the new enrichment step and its stated trigger.
evidence.period_fit: Immediate late-2022 escalation after multilateral censure
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level nuclear escalation under Khamenei's top-level authority over the file.
contrary_evidence: Iran presented the move as a response to political pressure, not a move toward weaponization.
The report does not prove a direct Khamenei order, only state action under his system.
